title: Fence Painting & Staining in Micanopy, FL
description: Fence painting and staining in Micanopy, FL: picket fences, privacy fences, and gates cleaned, repaired, and coated to suit older homes and shaded yards.
h1: Fence Painting and Staining in Micanopy, FL
heroIntro: A fence is often the first thing people see in front of an older home. We repair and repaint or stain it so it looks right with the house and holds up to shade and humidity.

questions: Should a fence in front of an older house be painted or stained?
How do you keep fence posts from rotting in the shade?
Can you match my fence color to my house trim?

sections.h2: A fence that fits the house
body: On a pre-war Micanopy home, a painted fence along the front yard can frame the house the way trim frames a window. A peeling, leaning, or mildew-streaked one does the opposite. In back yards, wood privacy fences take the same humidity and shade as everything else under the oaks, and they rot from the bottom up when moisture never gets a chance to leave.
Our fence painting in Micanopy, FL looks at both jobs: the fence as part of the home's appearance, and the fence as wood that needs protection.

Fences also sit right where the sprinklers, leaf piles, and mulch beds are. That combination keeps the lowest few inches of every board and post wet, so the bottom of the fence is always where we start our inspection, not the top.

A fence that has been painted before usually stays painted. We scrape it to a sound edge, spot-prime bare wood, and apply 100% acrylic, often in a color tied to the house trim. Bare, weathered, or previously stained wood is usually better with a penetrating stain, which soaks in and fades gradually instead of peeling. Vinyl fences can be cleaned and, where the surface is sound, coated with a suitable product.
If the history of your fence is a mystery, we figure it out on site before recommending a system.

bullets: Clean off mildew, algae, and leaf staining, then let the wood dry
Check posts and bottom rails for soft wood where moisture collects
Replace broken or rotted pickets and boards; re-fasten loose ones
Pull back vines and plants and protect beds from drips and overspray
Spray and back-brush stain, or brush and roll paint on detailed pickets
body: Gates and the posts that carry them take the most wear. We check hinges and latches, look for soft wood at the base of each post, and give the gate frame extra coats where hands and weather hit it hardest.

Many Micanopy owners paint the fence when they repaint the house, so colors match and prep overlaps. See residential painting in Micanopy for the bigger project, or color consultation if you are choosing new trim and fence colors together. For more on sun and weather damage to fencing in our region, read treating damaged wood fences in Alachua County. Product details are on our deck and fence staining page.

faqs.q: Should my picket fence be painted or stained?
faqs.a: If it has been painted before, it usually stays painted. Bare or weathered wood is often better with penetrating stain, which will not peel.

faqs.q: Can you match the fence to my house trim?
faqs.a: Yes. We can match from a chip, a door, or a leftover can and show a full-size drawdown first.

faqs.q: Do you replace rotted fence boards?
faqs.a: Yes. Replacement of pickets, boards, and rails is part of prep and is listed on the estimate.
